title: Feedback bottleneck mosaic and prioritized probe playbook
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is a compact, action-oriented synthesis of customer feedback we collected across CS tickets, sales calls, and field interviews in May–June 2027. The framing here is a 'bottleneck mosaic' — we map recurring customer friction to the narrowest operational or UX constraint, then propose small probes (experiments) that can validate root causes quickly.

Why this is different: many prior digests list asks by topic; this doc maps asks to the single bottleneck that, if eased, unlocks multiple asks. Focus is on high ROI patches (<= 3 sprint work) and one medium effort experiment to inform roadmap.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Primary bottlenecks observed: 1) onboarding friction for Private deployments (networking/KMS), 2) opaque per-request billing in hosted API and Dedicated, 3) model-fallback surprises during capacity throttles, 4) lack of quick dev-mode observability for reranking/embeddings.
- High-impact quick probes: automated KMS checklist + guided VPC test (owner: Solutions Eng), per-route token heatmap in Console (owner: Console PM), fallback transparency header + opt-out flag (owner: Serving Runtime).
- Medium experiment: synthetic workload lab to reproduce Dedicated burst failures (cross-team: infra + serving-runtime).

Raw signal snippets (representative quotes):
- "We spent 2 days just trying to get a KMS key to talk to the control plane — docs had 3 different env var names." — enterprise security lead
- "When the model falls back, our app gets short truncated responses and the user loses trust. We didn't even know a fallback happened." — platform engineer at SaaS mid-market customer
- "Token billing on multi-round chats is fuzzy — we can't easily tell which route or model caused most of the cost spike." — growth product manager

Bottleneck mapping (mosaic):
1) Private onboarding network/KMS mismatch
   - Symptom cluster: long trial setup times, repeated support tickets, legal hold-ups
   - Root-bottleneck hypothesis: install guide assumes uniform cloud IAM patterns; we have inconsistent CLI flags and missing 'dry-run' diagnostics for KMS endpoints
   - Proposed probes (quick):
     * 'KMS compatibility checklist' template for SEs + guided CLI dry-run command that validates keys/endpoints and prints user-friendly remediation steps (1 week SE + 1 week docs)
     * VPC connectivity simulator: small containerized runner customers can run that mimics our control-plane handshake (2 weeks infra + SE)
   - Success metric: onboarding time (first inference) reduced from median 4 days -> 1 day for pilot customers; #support-tickets for KMS down 50% after rollout

2) Per-request billing opacity (hosted & dedicated)
   - Symptom cluster: cost surprises on monthly invoice, inability to attribute spikes to routes/models/prompts
   - Root-bottleneck hypothesis: telemetry is captured but not surfaced at the token-level in an actionable console view; alerts are coarse-grained
   - Proposed probes (quick):
     * Console widget: per-route token heatmap (24h, 7d) + top-3 contributing prompts (backend + Console team, 2 sprints)
     * Slack alert prototype for sudden per-route token rate > X% (1 sprint)
   - Success metric: number of cost-related CS escalations drops 40%; pilot customers can triage cost incident in <30m

3) Undisclosed model fallback behavior
   - Symptom cluster: apps receiving shorter/less-reliable outputs during peak, customers unaware fallback replaced chosen model
   - Root-bottleneck hypothesis: smart routing performs silent fallbacks without clear metadata returned to client; SDKs discard fallback headers for convenience
   - Proposed probes (quick + low-risk):
     * Add 'x-rdwd-fallback' response header with model-id and reason; add SDK opt-in flag to surface fallback events to application logs (1 sprint serving-runtime)
     * Add 'fallback-visibility' toggle in Console per-key (can be enabled for pilot)
   - Success metric: number of incidents tagged as 'unexpected fallback' drops 70%; customers can instrument alerting on fallback headers

4) Dev-mode observability missing for embeddings and reranking
   - Symptom cluster: long debugging loops on retrieval/rerank relevance; customers rebuild local traces instead of using Console
   - Root-bottleneck hypothesis: Console traces are aggregated and lose per-token or per-candidate scores needed to reproduce ranking decisions
   - Proposed probes:
     * Developer trace export (ndjson) with candidate scores and prompt snapshot for a configurable sample rate (Console + SDK, 3 weeks)
     * Quick-start rerank-debugger notebook tied to SDKs showing end-to-end flow (solutions + DX, 1 week)
   - Success metric: time-to-reproduce-relevance-issue < 1 hour for pilot customers

Prioritization rubrics used here:
- Business impact: frequency of ask * customer tier weight (enterprise > mid-market > startup)
- Effort: quick (<= 2 dev weeks, docs + SE), medium (2–8 dev weeks), large (> 8 weeks)
- Risk: cross-team coordination, security, or data sensitivity concerns

Prioritized action lanes (short list):
- Lane A (Immediate, quick wins):
  1) KMS compatibility checklist + CLI dry-run (quick) — owner SE: Diego Martín — req: minimal infra support
  2) Fallback visibility header + SDK opt-in (quick) — owner: Serving Runtime PM: Sofia Reynolds
  3) Per-route token heatmap prototype in Console (1–2 sprints) — owner: Console PM: Maya Chen
- Lane B (Validate with experiment):
  1) Dedicated burst repro lab + stress test to capture routing/fallback thresholds (medium) — owner: Infra + Serving Runtime — deliverable: runbook + telemetry capture
- Lane C (Post-probe/roadmap candidates):
  1) VPC connectivity simulator as part of self-serve Private onboarding (medium)
  2) Developer trace export for reranking (medium)

Suggested owners, blockers, and handoffs (practical notes):
- SEs (Solutions Eng) should own KMS checklist creation and run pilot installs with 3 at-risk customers (Legal & Sec review required).
- Serving-runtime should own fallback header change but coordinate with SDK/DX to prevent breaking consumers (toggle behind feature flag).
- Console team owns visualization work; Console will need lightweight API endpoints for token breakdown (instrumentation ticket to Observability).

Low-effort quick fixes (<= 3 days):
- Consolidate CLI env var names in a single FAQ doc and add cross-links from the Private onboarding page.
- Add a 'why did my model change' snippet to hosted API error page (static content) pointing to CS flow.
- Create a one-page 'Cost spike triage checklist' for CS to hand to customers during incidents.

Open questions and uncertainties (notes to self):
- Do we have privacy constraints on surfacing top contributing prompts in Console? Need legal check (Maya action).
- Telemetry retention vs cost: per-token heatmaps may increase telemetry volume — what retention window is acceptable for pilot? (Infra + Observability)
- Can we simulate Dedicated burst conditions safely in prod-like infra without violating SLA agreements with other customers? (Infra risk review)

Pilot candidates (customers to invite):
- 'NimbusMail' (mid-market): heavy reranking; interested in trace export
- 'FinSight' (enterprise): strict KMS/KMS onboarding friction, good candidate for KMS checklist pilot
- 'ShopGrid' (startup): saw unexpected fallback events; will try fallback header opt-in

Next steps (for this doc):
- Week 0: sync with SEs and Console PM (owner: Aisha) to confirm scope for KMS checklist + token heatmap prototype
- Week 1: ship CLI dry-run and consolidated KMS FAQ; enable fallback header behind flag in staging
- Week 2–4: run Dedicated burst lab with Infra, collect telemetry, and decide roadmap commitment

Appendix: quick timeline estimate (rough)
- CLI dry-run + FAQ: 1 week docs + 1 dev day (SE + minimal infra)
- Fallback header + SDK opt-in: 1 sprint (serving-runtime + SDK)
- Token heatmap prototype: 2 sprints (console + observability)
- Dedicated burst lab: 3–4 weeks (infra + serving-runtime + SRE)

Contact / owner notes:
Aisha Patel (CS lead) — primary owner of this synthesis. Ping in #cs-field-signals and add to Confluence page once probe lanes are agreed.

---
Embedded quick checklist for SE handoff (copyable):
1) Before onboarding call: ask for KMS type, cloud provider, and whether HSM is needed.
2) Run: rdwd-cli kms-check --key-uri <URI> --dry-run  (returns friendly remediation steps)
3) If it fails: capture logs, escalate to infra with tag JIRA-ENG-4321 and include customer-id

End of doc.
